# 5 Key Investment Strategies To Learn Before Trading

Choosing a stock market strategy that fits your portfolio objectives and skills [...] Consider your investment vehicles. Cash accounts can be immediately withdrawn, but often have the greatest consequences. Accounts like 401ks can't be touched without fees until you retire and have more limited options, but your company may match your investment. Different types of IRAs also have various levels of flexibility. [...] Once you've answered the strategic questions above, you'll want to learn the basics of investing: how to read stock charts, etc., picking some of your favorite companies, and analyzing their financial statements. You'll also need to keep up to date with recent news about industries you're interested in investing in so you're not making uninformed decisions.

### Important

Determine how much you can invest: Before you begin investing, you should have enough money set aside to cover basic needs, like everyday expenses or an emergency. It’s also a good idea to tackle high-interest debt first, as the interest charged could outweigh the gains of your investments. [...] ### Assists with decision-making

An investment strategy helps you think about your financial decisions before you act. You weigh potential gains against other factors, such as access to money and tax considerations. When you consider all of the variables, you factor in how to balance risk and growth potential as you choose investments that fit your goals.

### Creates long-term financial plans [...] Here are five types of investment strategies used by investors. You can pick one or combine several to help you build a balanced portfolio that aligns with your financial goals and comfort level.

### 1. Buy-and-hold investing

Through the investment strategy known as “dollar cost averaging,” you can protect yourself from the risk of investing all of your money at the wrong time by following a consistent pattern of adding new money to your investment over a long period of time.  By making regular investments with the same amount of money each time, you will buy more of an investment when its price is low and less of the investment when its price is high.
